clarifications: What if the string is empty? Return true.
Can there be any characters other than parentheses? No, only '(', ')', '{', '}', '[' and ']'.
What should be returned? Return true if the string is valid, false otherwise.
expectedApproaches: Use a stack to track open parentheses, O(n) time and O(n) space.
Use a counter for each type of parenthesis, but this fails to handle order.
solutions: Initialize an empty stack. Iterate over each character in the string. If it's an opening bracket, push it onto the stack. If it's a closing bracket, check if the stack is empty (if so, return false) and if the top of the stack is the matching opening bracket (if not, return false). Pop the stack in this case. Finally, return true if the stack is empty, false otherwise.
commonMistakes: Forgetting to check if the stack is empty before popping.
Not checking if the stack is empty at the end of the iteration.
Using counters instead of a stack, which fails to check order.

hintLadder.text: What data structure can help you match open and close brackets efficiently?
Consider using a stack to keep track of open brackets.
Push open brackets onto a stack and pop when you encounter a matching close bracket.
